comparator.name: Psychology
comparator.sourceNotes: The dated 2026–2027 guide controls this 180-EC pathway. The generic registry target includes English and Dutch teaching. Brain and Cognition is retained as the first detailed numbered public option and first dated study path, chosen independently of UCR fit. Its four named courses total 30 EC. The third year selects Behavioural Research Toolbox, the Brain and Cognition thesis, Consciousness: From Theory to the Clinic in period one, Psychology and AI in period two, and thirty genuinely open optional credits. Completing the full first year, research participation and common Year-2 courses meets specialisation entry; completing its full thirty credits including the toolbox meets the third-year methods threshold. The thesis follows the first part of the methods course. Zero-credit academic practicals, research participation and five colloquium points remain compulsory and are not added to the credit total.
components: Work and Organisational Psychology & Social Psychology
Academic-skills practicals and research participation are compulsory without additional credits. All earlier reading and writing assignments must be passed before the first-year thesis.
This pathway completes all 60 first-year credits, including Research Methods & Statistics and research participation, before Year 2. The common courses require 48 or 60 first-year credits.
One coherent Brain and Cognition specialisation is selected. Its four courses require the full first year and Scientific and Statistical Reasoning, completed before this semester.
B&C Toolbox: Experimental and Neuroscientific Methods
The 12-EC toolbox integrates behavioural experiments, neuroscience methods, data analysis, experimental design and Python programming.
Entry requires the full first year, Scientific and Statistical Reasoning, Psychological Research and at least 18 EC of the specialisation, including its toolbox. All are completed in Year 2.

The 12-EC empirical thesis follows the first part of Behavioural Research Toolbox. The earlier requirements and at least 18 specialisation credits must be passed. Five colloquium points must also be obtained; they add no separate degree credits. Students conduct supervised group research and write individual empirical reports.
Current Topics: Consciousness: From Theory to the Clinic
Selected from the restricted period-one Current Topics menu: consciousness research through psychological, neuroscientific and clinical approaches.
Selected from the restricted period-two Current Topics menu: the relationship between psychological science and AI. The full first year is required; prior AI or programming knowledge is not.

Thirty EC remain genuinely open for a second specialisation, minor, exchange or an approved coherent course package. Individually chosen packages need Examination Board approval, research-university level, no overlap with Psychology and at most 12 first-year EC. No specific minor, course package or host is assumed.

core: Psychological foundations of thinking, emotion, motivation, behaviour and social relationships
Brain, cognition, perception and memory with the selected Brain and Cognition specialisation
Empirical research, statistics, measurement, experimental design and independent psychological research
Human development, mental health, clinical assessment and psychological disorders
adjacent: Clinical, developmental and neuropsychological assessment and intervention
Psychology of organisations, work, social influence and leadership
Psychological methods, behavioural data and measurement
questions: How do social influence and cognitive load shape behaviour and decisions?
How can psychological science investigate mental health and development?
How can psychologists design and analyse research on workplace behaviour?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: develops scholarly reading, academic writing, research questions, reflection and collaborative practice as the common first-year foundation

uses psychology-informed biases, heuristics, framing and experiments to examine departures from traditional economic decision models; this directly supports the social-decision strand within the scope of its description
develops measurement, empirical design, sampling, statistics and a student data-collection project as foundations for psychological research
examines self-leadership, personality and emotional intelligence in group dynamics, with reflective leadership cases and a personal development plan rather than clinical diagnosis
examines leadership communication, persuasion, emotional intelligence, culture and ethics through leader interviews, advisory analysis and rhetorical practice
examines emotion regulation, belonging, identity and psychological safety in leadership, with an original quantitative psychological survey, measurement, data analysis and empirical reporting
directly examines personality, perception, emotions, motivation, group dynamics, leadership, culture and organisational change, with research plans and a systematic literature review
examines bargaining, framing, power, emotions, trust and culture through negotiation theory and repeated simulations, implementing social decision-making in practice
develops data cleaning, transformation, visualisation and an applied research workflow in R, materially supporting empirical behavioural inquiry

develops regression, classification, prediction, model evaluation and statistical learning on real data, supporting the cognitive and behavioural-data focus without claiming a psychology-specific AI course
develops ethical theories and reasoned analysis of moral problems as a complementary basis for evaluating choices in assessment, treatment and health
examines mind, consciousness, identity, physicalism and neuropsychological cases through philosophical argument, complementing empirical cognition
examines theories of emotion and their relationship to knowledge, decisions, ethics and social life through philosophical analysis, complementing empirical psychological accounts
examines socialisation, interaction, inequality and institutions as social mechanisms shaping individual and group behaviour, complementing the psychological explanations
develops qualitative research design, interviews, observation, coding and interpretation for studying human experience and social behaviour
examines modern sociological explanations of social order, inequality, identity and institutions as a structural complement to social and organisational psychology
examines civil society, solidarity, trust and exclusion as mechanisms of collective life, supporting the social-group focus alongside individual psychological explanation
develops epidemiological designs, bias, confounding and causal interpretation for evaluating disease patterns and health evidence; mental-health applications are not a separate taught specialism
examines drug action, kinetics, metabolism, toxicity and pharmacogenomics, including nervous-system drugs and a psychoactive-drug research proposal, supporting the health and mental-disorder strand
connects organ regulation and dysfunction to endocrine, nervous-system and other disease mechanisms through clinical cases, providing a biomedical complement to psychological disorder
examines comparative neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, animal behaviour, sleep and rhythms, with biological explanations of behaviour and laboratory introductions
examines neural mechanisms of sensory information processing and goal-directed action through cognitive-neuroscience and neuropsychological approaches
examines attention, memory, emotion, cognitive control and consciousness through neural function and dysfunction, an attentional-blink experiment and a research proposal
examines neural and psychological mechanisms of language acquisition, comprehension and production, language impairments and experimental approaches within the scope of its description
introduces cells, biomolecules, metabolism, heredity and gene expression as biological foundations for the neural and health dimensions of psychology
introduces neural signalling, brain organisation, development, learning and behavioural/neuroscience research as direct foundations for brain-behaviour study
examines homeostasis, neuroendocrine signalling and integrated organ-system regulation, giving the clinical/health option a biological account of brain-body interaction
directly examines social cognition, attitudes, influence, groups and interpersonal behaviour through empirical studies and a research proposal
develops experimental design, multivariable statistical models and data-analysis reporting in health and behavioural research
directly examines mental disorders through biological, psychological, social and cultural explanations, case analysis and a structured literature study
examines stress, symptoms, illness and health behaviour through biological, psychological and social interactions

directly examines psychological tests, interviews, assessment and major therapy approaches, with introductory skills training and a psychodiagnostic case report; it confers no professional qualification
develops systematic review and quantitative meta-analysis, effect sizes, heterogeneity, bias and research reporting in behavioural and medical inquiry
directly examines physical, cognitive, social and emotional development across the lifespan, with biological/environmental influences and a life-story study
examines youth radicalisation, developmental risk and protective factors, belonging and social-emotional learning, applying research in educational prevention materials
develops rhetorical analysis, argument and persuasive speaking as applied social communication, without substituting for psychologist interviewing training

examines how grammar, discourse, schemas, modality and construal shape interpretation, principally in literary texts, as a linguistic complement to social communication rather than workplace-psychology training
examines coactive persuasion, framing, argumentation and cognitive shortcuts through communication research and community projects on behaviour change

alternatives.label: Psychology, brain & cognition
alternatives.concept: Study behaviour and mental processes through social, developmental, clinical and organisational psychology, with a sustained brain-and-cognition emphasis. Neuroscience, perception, memory, language, empirical statistics and data analysis support this focus; philosophy examines mind and emotion as complementary conceptual questions.
alternatives.labelReason: Study behaviour and mental processes through social, developmental, clinical and organisational psychology, with a sustained brain-and-cognition emphasis. Neuroscience, perception, memory, language, empirical statistics and data analysis support this focus; philosophy examines mind and emotion as complementary conceptual questions.
progression: Every assigned term and earlier formal prerequisite is checked against the current workbook. Introductory psychology precedes advanced psychological methods; Neurobiology precedes Higher Order Functions and statistics precedes meta-analysis. Psycholinguistics is placed in its only planned term, after Brain and Behavior and concurrently with Neurobiology. Data foundations precede machine learning where selected.

alternatives.label: Clinical, developmental & mental-health psychology
alternatives.concept: Study development, mental disorder, psychological assessment and treatment approaches alongside health psychology, neuroscience and empirical research. Physiology, epidemiology, nervous-system pharmacology, disease mechanisms and ethics give a biological and health-related perspective. This programme provides academic study and introductory skills, without professional clinical qualification.

Physiology, epidemiology, nervous-system pharmacology, disease mechanisms and ethics give a biological and health-related perspective. This programme provides academic study and introductory skills, without professional clinical qualification.
progression: Every assigned term and earlier formal prerequisite is checked against the current workbook. Introductory psychology precedes advanced psychological methods; Neurobiology precedes Higher Order Functions and statistics precedes meta-analysis. Psycholinguistics is placed in its only planned term, after Brain and Behavior and concurrently with Neurobiology. Data foundations precede machine learning where selected.
alternatives.distinctness: Physiology, epidemiology, pharmacology, mechanisms of disease and ethics replace organisational psychology, statistical learning, persuasion and philosophical study of mind and emotion. This sustains a health and clinical focus rather than the closest option’s broader cognitive, computational and organisational response.

alternatives.label: Social & organisational psychology
alternatives.concept: Study social influence, individual and group behaviour, emotion, motivation and organisations through psychology, leadership and empirical research. Negotiation, behavioural economics, persuasion and linguistic analysis examine how people interpret messages and make decisions in social and workplace settings.
alternatives.labelReason: Study social influence, individual and group behaviour, emotion, motivation and organisations through psychology, leadership and empirical research. Negotiation, behavioural economics, persuasion and linguistic analysis examine how people interpret messages and make decisions in social and workplace settings.
progression: Every assigned offering and earlier formal prerequisite is checked against the current workbook. Brain and Behavior precedes dependent psychology; Research Methods & Statistics precedes experimental statistics, behavioural economics and leadership courses; statistics precedes meta-analysis. Introductory leadership precedes the later organisational and negotiation work.
alternatives.distinctness: Leadership, organisational psychology, negotiation, behavioural economics, persuasion, sociology and linguistic interpretation give this programme a sustained social and workplace focus. It replaces the other options’ extended neuroscience, biological and health sequences rather than merely relabelling shared psychology courses.

candidates.label: Psychological methods and behavioural data
candidates.reason: The methods direction is well supported, but the three-alternative maximum is reached; quantitative and experimental methods already run through the included programmes.

candidates.label: Clinical neuropsychology
candidates.reason: Clinical Neuropsychology is a valid Dutch-language direction within this bilingual generic target. The maximum of three is reached; no separate implementation or no-match judgment is claimed.

routeSelection.basis: The bilingual generic Psychology target has seven dated study paths. Brain and Cognition is the first detailed numbered public option and the first dated study path; no default is claimed. Retain this neutral ordering independently of UCR fit. Clinical Neuropsychology is Dutch-only and remains a valid interest direction for this bilingual target, but is not the chosen pathway.

selection.assessment: The closest response combines substantial psychology, cognition and research with actual data and organisational methods. The clinical/health option and social/organisational option were then tested as coherent programme-interest priorities and each meets qualitative distinctness and the pairwise thirty-EC floor. Psychological Methods and Clinical Neuropsychology remain supported but unattempted after the maximum of three; neither is declared infeasible.

blocks: Psychology, cognition, social behaviour and research
Both develop empirical design, measurement, statistical testing and data analysis. UCR applies these across disciplines; UvA establishes the psychology-specific sequence.

Both involve psychological measurement, original data collection, quantitative analysis and empirical reporting. UCR studies leadership-related survey questions; UvA additionally constructs a psychological test and provides its prescribed test-theory sequence.

Both substantively examine statistical prediction and machine-learning approaches to data. UCR develops regression, classification and model evaluation in depth; UvA introduces behavioural big data, latent variables, network analysis and prediction from a psychology perspective.

Both examine the nature of mind, physical explanation and conceptual problems behind psychological science. UCR emphasises philosophy of mind; UvA also examines the history and general foundations of psychology.
Both examine neural anatomy, physiology and mechanisms underlying behaviour. UvA builds explicitly from molecular/cellular mechanisms to cortical and subcortical networks and research techniques.
Both examine sensory processing and the neural relationship between perception and action. UvA also addresses attention, multisensory integration and consciousness.

Both examine memory and emotion through cognitive neuroscience and neural dysfunction. UvA also gives substantial explicit coverage to language, while UCR includes attention, control and consciousness.
Both introduce brain organisation, mental processes and the relationship between neural function and behaviour. UvA also surveys the whole discipline of psychology.
Both substantively examine social cognition, attitudes, influence and group processes. The combined UvA component additionally covers work and organisational psychology.
Both develop empirical research design, statistical models and critical interpretation of psychological findings. UvA explicitly integrates scientific argumentation.
Both examine psychological disorder, symptoms, explanatory models and clinical perspectives. UvA additionally provides a distinct neurological-disorder and neuropsychology introduction.

Both develop psychological interviewing, reflection and interpersonal assessment skills. UCR embeds introductory practice in clinical assessment and therapy; UvA provides a dedicated general psychological-communication practical.
Both examine physical, cognitive, emotional and social development and biological/environmental influences across the lifespan.
Other dedicated Psychology requirements and open choice
No selected UCR course is a separately credited first-year psychology thesis.

Selected courses contribute experimental design, cognitive experiments and data methods elsewhere, but none reproduces this dedicated combination of neuroscientific measurement, behavioural paradigms and Python experiment/programming practice.

Advanced statistics, meta-analysis and computational study are represented elsewhere. None is counted again as this dedicated course in simulation studies, mathematical cognitive-task models and Python/PsychoPy experiment construction.
The 12-EC Brain and Cognition empirical thesis is compulsory at UvA. Optional UCR independent research is shown separately outside scheduled credits.
Higher cognitive study has its strongest placement with Memory, Language and Emotion. No additional course is counted as this dedicated experimental, neuroscientific and clinical consciousness topic.

The strongest selected statistical-learning relationship is placed with Behavioural Data Science. No additional course is counted as this integrated account of AI and psychology, their shared history and contemporary applications and ethics.
The thirty-credit optional profile is genuinely open; no particular minor, exchange host or course package is invented.

notes.text: UCR can combine substantial psychological, cognitive, social, biological and data study. UvA provides a prescribed Psychology degree, specialist methods and practicals, and a compulsory Brain and Cognition thesis. The course relationships shown are partial; introductory clinical study at UCR does not confer professional qualification.

audience.programmeDescription: Psychology at UvA studies behaviour and mental processes through research, statistics and broad psychological foundations. This example follows the Brain and Cognition specialisation, with named current topics on consciousness and AI, an empirical thesis and thirty credits of open choice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines broad psychology with neuroscience, cognition and empirical data methods. Two further options emphasise clinical and health questions or social behaviour and organisations. UvA provides a more prescribed disciplinary and specialist practical sequence; the partial relationships do not reproduce its required thesis or confer clinical qualification.
